title: Older yet faster: Representational development explains accelerated semantic processing in older adults.
title_zh: 年长却更快：表征发展解释了老年人语义处理的加速
abstract: Slower responses in older age are often taken as evidence for cognitive decline, yet they may also stem from representational changes shaped by lifelong learning. Building on the information-accumulation perspective on aging, we argue that behavioral change across the lifespan can arise from representational systems continuously updated through learning from the environment. This view predicts that aging may bring both benefits and costs: Performance improves when task demands are congruent with accumulated knowledge but declines when they conflict. We provide convergent evidence for this account across three studies, each comprising the following components. First, in tasks requiring participants to access word meanings (i.e., when task demands were congruent with representation), we found that older adults (70-80 years old) exhibited faster semantic processing speed than younger adults (18-25 years old), a finding that cannot be explained by decline-based accounts. Second, we traced this processing advantage to systematic changes in older adults' conceptual representations inferred from semantic rating tasks. Third, using learning simulation models, we demonstrated how such representational changes could emerge naturally from cumulative language experience. Replications across different samples, task requirements, and word stimuli strengthen the robustness of these findings. Finally, we identified a boundary condition: When learned representations contain information incongruent with task demands, older adults' greater learning experience not only attenuates their representational changes but also reduces processing-speed advantage. Altogether, our research challenges the explanatory framework of cognitive aging that emphasizes decline and compensation, advancing a more balanced view grounded in representational development and lifelong learning. abstract_zh: 老年人较慢的反应常被视为认知衰退的证据，但也可能源于由终身学习塑造的表征变化。基于老龄化的信息累积视角，我们论证行为终身变化可以源于通过环境学习不断更新的表征系统。这一观点预测，衰老可能带来利弊：当任务需求与积累的知识一致时，表现会提高；当它们冲突时，则会下降。我们在三项研究中提供了该观点的收敛证据，每项研究均包括以下组成部分。首先，在要求参与者获取词义（即任务需求与表征一致）的任务中，我们发现70-80岁的老年人比18-25岁的年轻人表现出更快的语义处理速度，这一发现无法由基于衰退的解释说服。其次，我们通过语义评估任务追踪了老年人概念表征的系统性变化。第三，利用学习模拟模型，我们展示了此类表征变化如何自然地从累积的语言经验中产生。跨不同年本、任务要求和词刺激的重复验证加强了这些发现的健壮性。最后，我们确定了一个边界条件：当学习到的表征包含与任务需求不一致的信息时，老年人更丰富的学习经验不仅抑制了其表征变化，也降低了处理速度优势。总之，我们的研究挑战了强调衰退和补偿的老龄化解释框架，推进了基于表征发展和终身学习的更平衡视角。（PsycInfo 数据库记录 (c) 2026 APA，版权所有）
